URL: https://www.iea.org/commentaries/how-global-oil-supplies-have-readjusted-to-help-fill-the-huge-gap-left-by-the-strait-of-hormuz-shock
IEA commentary, published 22 June 2026. Authors: Toril Bosoni, Head of Oil Industry and Markets Division; David Martin, Senior Oil Market Analyst; Rebecca Schulz, Senior Oil Market Analyst.
Transit volumes: flows through the Strait of Hormuz fell "from around 20 million barrels per day prior to the conflict to an average of 2.7 million barrels per day in March, April and May."
Cumulative oil supply loss from Middle Eastern producers exceeded 1.3 billion barrels during the crisis.
Emergency stocks: "the largest ever release of their emergency oil stocks - 400 million barrels - to help offset the disruptions." By May this delivered roughly 2.5 million b/d to markets.
